title: Nvidia and Wall Street’s Biggest Titans Just Struck a $500 Billion Deal. Here’s What’s In It For Both Sides
excerpt: Jensen Huang just recruited six of the most powerful names in finance to solve the one problem threatening to put a ceiling on AI growth, and Nvidia is not s...
content_html:
AJ Tiarsmith

Tue, August 11, 2026 at 4:36 AM PDT 5 min read

Quick Read

  • NVDA acts as matchmaker in a $500B AI financing consortium, contributing no capital while connecting customers to Wall Street funding.

  • Goldman Sachs and Apollo join four other Wall Street giants as passive funders, gaining a steady pipeline of Nvidia-vetted AI borrowers.

  • With hyperscalers set to spend $3.5T on AI infrastructure by 2028, this consortium is Huang's insurance policy for $91B in Q2 revenue.

  • It sounds nuts, but SoFi1 is giving new Active Invest users up to $3,000 in stock for a limited time, and all it takes is a $50 deposit to get started.2 See for yourself (Sponsor)

The largest capital pool ever assembled around a single technology theme just got a new front door. On CNBC yesterday, co-anchor Becky Quick reported that "Nvidia is coming together with some of the biggest names on Wall Street to put together half a trillion of independent financing, to kind of push AI forward, to build the AI infrastructure out." The story, initially broken by the Financial Times, positions NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) at the center of a financing consortium designed to unclog what CEO Jensen Huang has long flagged as the single biggest constraint on AI adoption: capital.

Crucially, "Nvidia is not putting up any of the money. This isn't a circular deal. This is Nvidia basically playing matchmaker to bring together some of these names that have already been pretty active when it comes to financing for some of these deals." Nvidia will identify customers that need financing to build out AI capacity and connect them with the pledging partners.

Why Huang Wants a Matchmaker

Nvidia's Q1 FY2027 report already showed a business straining against the outer edge of what customers can finance. Data Center revenue reached $75.25 billion, up 92% year over year, and total supply commitments swelled to $119.0 billion. Huang has framed the moment as "the buildout of AI factories, the largest infrastructure expansion in human history" (see the company's Q1 FY27 earnings release).

SoFi Active Invest is offering a limited-time promotion. Open an account, fund it with $50 or more, and you could receive up to $3,000 in complimentary stock for Active Invest accounts. See for yourself by clicking here now. (Sponsor)

Quick captured the logic neatly: "Jensen Huang has for a long time been looking for bottlenecks that would prevent AI from reaching its full growth potential. I think this is a bottleneck that they've identified and said, here's a way that we're going to go about addressing it." With hyperscalers projected to spend approximately $3.5 trillion between 2026 and 2028 on data centers, chips, power, and real estate, financing gaps could throttle Nvidia's chip demand well before compute demand tops out. Shares closed at $217.55, up 16.79% year to date.

  • 到 2028 年，超大规模企业将在人工智能基础设施上花费 3.5T 美元，该联盟是黄仁勋的第二季度收入 91B 美元的保险单。

有史以来围绕单一技术主题聚集的最大资本池刚刚有了新的大门。 昨天在 CNBC 上，联合主持人贝基·奎克 (Becky Quick) 报道称，“英伟达正在与华尔街一些最知名的公司合作，筹集 5 万亿美元的独立融资，以推动人工智能向前发展，建设人工智能基础设施。” 这个故事最初由英国《金融时报》报道，将 NVIDIA（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）定位为一个融资财团的核心，该财团旨在疏通 CEO 黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 长期以来所说的人工智能采用的最大限制：资本。

至关重要的是，“英伟达没有投入任何资金。 这不是一个循环交易。 英伟达基本上是在扮演牵线搭桥的角色，将一些在为其中一些交易融资时已经非常活跃的名字聚集在一起。” 英伟达将确定需要融资来建设人工智能能力的客户，并将他们与承诺合作伙伴联系起来。

黄为什么要找媒人

Nvidia 的 2027 财年第一季度报告已经显示，其业务在客户融资方面面临压力。 数据中心收入达到 752.5 亿美元，同比增长 92%，供应承诺总额增至 1190 亿美元。 黄把这一时刻描述为“人工智能工厂的建设，人类历史上最大规模的基础设施扩张”（参见该公司 2027 财年第一季度财报）。

SoFi Active Invest 正在提供限时促销活动。 开设一个账户，注入 50 美元或更多资金，您就可以为 Active Invest 账户获得高达 3,000 美元的免费股票。 立即点击此处亲自查看。 （赞助）

奎克巧妙地抓住了这个逻辑：“黄仁勋长期以来一直在寻找阻碍人工智能充分发挥其增长潜力的瓶颈。 我认为这是他们已经发现的瓶颈，并表示，我们将采取一种方法来解决这个问题。” 预计 2026 年至 2028 年间，超大规模企业将在数据中心、芯片、电力和房地产方面花费约 3.5 万亿美元，融资缺口可能会在计算需求达到顶峰之前抑制 Nvidia 的芯片需求。 股价收于 217.55 美元，年初至今上涨 16.79%。
